title: Reddit's traffic is down 13%, partly thanks to AI Overviews
content:
New data sheds further light on Reddit's search traffic woes.
Reddit's traffic dipped 13% in global visits from October 2025 to October 2026, according to analytics firm Similarweb. The decline traffic sent to Reddit from Google search has driven Reddit to go (mostly) logged-in-only.
However, Reddit reported in a recent letter to shareholders that the number of weekly active uniques were up 16% year over year in October. That's a slightly different measurement than Similarweb's estimate. A spokesperson for Reddit told Business Insider that Reddit's reporting is based on daily and weekly active uniques rather than total visits.
Reddit's traffic has been hurt by the way people are increasingly going to chatbots for answers, and especially the way that Google increasingly shows people AI Overviews instead of a list of links.
In Reddit's recent Q3 earnings, CEO Steve Huffman said that Google AI Overviews "are not traffic drivers" and have led to a drop in search traffic to the site. In a letter to investors, he said that Google search traffic was "down meaningfully" and that if the trend continued it could lead to a low double-digit drop in unique visits.
Reddit's shift to a logged-in experience is because that's where its most lucrative, non-logged-in web traffic (the kind that took a dip). Huffman said: "Search referral trends do not determine our relevancy, and they do not define our future. Logged-in and app DAUq are our most valuable users, and they are our primary focus."
It wasn't always this way — in 2024, Reddit made a deal with Google to license itself for AI training at a time when Reddit's search traffic was surging thanks to Google.
Reddit's traffic shot up 39% from May 2023 to May 2024, according to Similarweb. But as AI Overviews have become more and more frequent and useful, Reddit's traffic has dipped.
Once the logged-in-only experience starts, web traffic will likely dip even more, since some people will get shut out from the site. But Reddit seems to be leaning into where it has the most value for people.
Just this week, the company announced it would be launching Reddit Reviews, which will organize user recommendations for products.

report.summary: Reddit’s global traffic fell 13% year over year as Google AI Overviews and chatbots reduce search referrals, pushing Reddit toward logged-in and app-focused use.
report.background: For years, Reddit benefited from Google search: its forum threads ranked well for niche queries, and a 2024 licensing deal let Google use Reddit content for AI training while search referrals surged. Similarweb data showed Reddit visits up 39% from May 2023 to May 2024. But the search industry has shifted toward AI-generated answers. Google’s AI Overviews increasingly summarize results at the top of the page, and chatbots like ChatGPT answer questions directly, both reducing clicks to publisher sites. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said AI Overviews “are not traffic drivers” and search traffic was “down meaningfully.” In response, Reddit is prioritizing logged-in users and its app, where engagement is more valuable and measurable, and is testing new products like Reddit Reviews. The tension is industry-wide: platforms that depended on search referrals must adapt as AI intermediaries capture attention.
key_points: Similarweb estimates Reddit’s global visits fell 13% from October 2025 to October 2026, with declining Google search referrals as a major cause. Reddit disputes the framing, saying weekly active uniques rose 16% year over year in October, based on daily and weekly active users rather than total visits.

Google AI Overviews and chatbots are changing how people find answers. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said AI Overviews “are not traffic drivers” and Google search traffic was “down meaningfully,” warning that continued declines could cause a low double-digit drop in unique visits.

Reddit is responding by pushing a mostly logged-in-only experience and focusing on its app. Huffman said logged-in and app daily active users are Reddit’s most valuable users and that search referral trends do not define its future, even if web traffic falls further.

The shift reverses Reddit’s recent search boom. A 2024 Google AI training licensing deal coincided with surging referrals, but AI-first search is now reducing clicks. Reddit is also launching Reddit Reviews to organize user product recommendations and deepen on-platform value.
report.impact: Reddit’s decline is a warning for the open web: if AI Overviews and chatbots answer questions without sending clicks, traffic-dependent platforms lose reach and ad inventory. For the AI industry, it strengthens the case for licensing deals and publisher partnerships, but also invites regulation and antitrust scrutiny over zero-click search. Developers should assume fewer search referrals and design for direct, logged-in, app, or community channels; content strategies must optimize for being cited by AI answers, not just ranked. Regular users may get faster answers, but more of the web could move behind logins or apps, reducing public access and making independent communities harder to find. Reddit’s pivot shows platforms may trade open-web visibility for higher-value engaged users.
report.tools: To track the shift, watch Similarweb and Google Search Console for referral data; use open-source analytics like Matomo, Plausible, or Umami to monitor traffic sources on your own site. For AI-search experimentation, try SearXNG (private meta-search), Perplexica (open-source AI answer engine), and Open WebUI (local chatbot interface). These help developers test how answer-first interfaces affect clicks and content discovery.
